<cite ref="Onkelos Exodus 18:16">Targ. O. Ex. XVIII, 16</cite> <he>דָּאֵינָא</he> ed. Berl. (Var. <he>דָּאִיְנָא</he>, <he>דָּאִינְנָא</he>, v. Berl. Targ. O. II, p. 25; Y. <cite ref="D00561"><he>דָּיֵינָא</he></cite>).—Ib. <he>מִידַן</he>, <he>מֵידוּן</he>. Targ. O. ib. 13 <cite ref="L00573"><he>לְמִידַן</he></cite> (ed. Berl. <he>לִמְדַּן</he>, Y. <he>למֵידוּן</he>); a. e.—Y. Snh. I, 18ᵃ bot. <he>יתיב דָּיֵין וכ׳</he> sat holding court single-handed.
<cite ref="Yoma 2a">Ib.</cite> <he>הוו דָּיְינִין קומי וכ׳</he> had a law-suit before &c.

<cite ref="Bava Batra 29a">B. Bath. 29ᵃ</cite>, v. <cite ref="D00561"><he>דַּיָּינָא</he></cite>; a. fr. [<cite ref="Shabbat 67b">Sabb. 67ᵇ</cite>, v. <cite ref="D00927"><he>דני</he></cite>.]—<he>דּוּן מִינָּהּ ומינה</he> judge from it and (all) from it, i.e. an analogy (v. <cite ref="C00553"><he>גְּזֵירָה</he></cite>) must be carried through all points so that the case deduced agrees throughout with the case from which the deduction has started, opp. <he>דון מינה ואוקי באתרה</he> judge from it and place the deduction back on its own basis, i.e. let the deduction won by analogy be regulated by the rules of the original case, e.g.
<cite ref="Shevuot 31a:19">Shebu. 31ᵃ</cite> an analogy between testimony and trust with reference to false oaths (<cite ref="Leviticus 5:1">Lev. V, 1</cite> sq., a. 21 sq.).
<cite ref="Yevamot 78b:9">Yeb. 78ᵇ</cite>; <cite ref="Bava Kamma 25b:12">B. Kam. 25ᵇ</cite>; a. fr.
<cite ref="Targum Jonathan on Exodus 15:12">Targ. Y. Ex. XV, 12</cite>; a. e.
<cite ref="Shevuot 32b:6">Shebu. 32ᵇ</cite> <he>היכי לִדַיְּינֵי דַיָּינֵי וכ׳</he> how shall the judges decide this case?; <cite ref="Shevuot 47a:9">ib. 47ᵃ</cite> <he>לִידַיְּינוּ</he>; a. e.
